record.title: microduck-top-head-shell — Pollen Robotics' published mesh `top_head_shell`, mesh-backed part
record.origin_why: the geometry is the vendor's own published sim asset, loaded unchanged (cecad.meshshelve, 2026-09-01). Not our design; usable to assemble, render, simulate and print; NOT licensed for sale (NC).
record.why: a loader: the mesh is the vendor's; whether it builds as a closed solid is read off bin/cad part:microduck-top-head-shell. MEASURED ABOUT THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF, 2026-09-03 (lane T): that command is not cheap on a shared machine. `ce-cad/bin/cad tools/build_mesh_loaders.py` — which runs this folder's own build() through cecad.triad.load and reports solids, shells, closedness, volume and bbox off the BUILT object — was started here at 22:57 on 2026-09-02 against fourteen mesh-backed folders and had consumed 131 minutes of CPU over 3 h 43 min of wall clock WITHOUT completing, on a Mac whose 1-minute load average ran 41-80 from other lanes' concurrent FreeCAD jobs. Part.from_mesh sewing a 20 000-triangle decimated mesh is the cost. So this folder's verdict is still CANNOT DETERMINE and the reason is now specific: the check has not been run to completion, not that nobody thought to run it. WHAT SETTLES IT: `ce-cad/bin/cad tools/build_mesh_loaders.py microduck-top-head-shell` on an idle machine, one slug at a time; the tool writes out/laneT/build-report.json and exits 1 if any folder produced neither a solid nor a shell.
